title: Lesson 17: Machine Learning Categories, Genetic Learning, and Perceptrons

slides.title: Machine learning has multiple category axes

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Lesson seventeen asks a more useful question than, what type of machine learning is this? A method can be classified simultaneously by the representation it changes, the feedback it receives, and the timing of its updates. One label is rarely enough.

focuses.phrase: Lesson seventeen asks a more useful question
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Lesson seventeen asks a more useful question
kinetics.label: Machine learning has multiple category axes

segments.label: Define
segments.text: We will compare symbolic structures with numeric adaptation, evolve expressions with genetic programming, calculate a neuron's weighted score, and train a perceptron from labeled mistakes. Different mechanisms become comparable when we ask the same three questions.

focuses.phrase: We will compare symbolic structures with numeric
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: By the end, explain what changes, what signal guides the change, when updates occur, and what the representation can express. That last capacity question explains why one perceptron handles AND but loses an argument with XOR.

focuses.phrase: By the end, explain what changes, what
focuses.label: Mechanism

slides.title: From categories to one trainable neuron

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: First, categorize the learner on three independent axes. Representation asks what form changes; feedback asks what teaching signal is available; timing asks whether updates use a fixed collection or arrive sequentially.

focuses.label: Frame

segments.label: Define

focuses.phrase: Second, watch genetic programming search expression trees
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Third, open one artificial neuron. Inputs are multiplied by weights, bias shifts the score, and activation converts that score to output. The arithmetic is small enough to calculate by hand, which is less dramatic than the word neuron sounds.

segments.text: Fourth, let a perceptron discover weights from examples. We will trace mistakes numerically, interpret the boundary geometrically, test XOR, and connect the hard threshold to smooth activations.

slides.title: A method occupies several categories at once

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: The representation axis asks what object is modified. A decision tree changes tests and branches. A perceptron changes numeric weights. K-means changes centroid geometry, and reinforcement learning commonly changes values or a policy.

focuses.phrase: The representation axis asks what object is
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: The representation axis asks what object is
kinetics.label: A method occupies several categories at once

segments.label: Define
segments.text: The feedback axis asks where guidance comes from. Supervised methods compare predictions with labels. Unsupervised methods seek structure without class labels. Reinforcement learning receives reward, often delayed, so the correct action is not written beside every state.

focuses.phrase: The feedback axis asks where guidance comes
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The timing axis asks when evidence changes the learner. Batch learning trains from a collected dataset. Online learning can update as examples arrive. Online-capable describes a mechanism, not a guarantee of good real-time decisions.

focuses.phrase: The timing axis asks when evidence changes
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: These axes are coordinates, not competing boxes. A perceptron is non-symbolic, supervised, and online-capable simultaneously. Genetic programming here uses numeric fitness to search symbolic-looking trees, supervised by targets, in batches.

focuses.phrase: These axes are coordinates, not competing boxes.
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: A useful test is to hold two axes fixed and change the third. A perceptron trained once on a stored file and one updated after every arriving label share representation and feedback but differ in timing. K-means and a supervised geometric classifier may both manipulate numeric geometry but differ in feedback. The axes stop superficial similarity from collapsing distinct mechanisms.

focuses.phrase: A useful test is to hold two
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Choose Decision tree
segments.text: A decision tree represents a prediction as a sequence of feature tests: each branch asks a question, and each leaf returns an answer. Labeled examples provide the feedback for choosing useful splits, and the full training set is usually revisited in batches while the tree is constructed.

focuses.phrase: A decision tree represents a prediction as
focuses.label: Choose Decision tree

segments.label: Choose Genetic programming
segments.text: Genetic programming represents candidate solutions as executable expression trees. It scores those programs with a fitness function, then repeatedly selects, crosses, and mutates them. Feedback arrives after evaluating candidates on a batch of examples, so learning behaves more like evolutionary search than a direct formula update.

focuses.phrase: Genetic programming represents candidate solutions as executable
focuses.label: Choose Genetic programming

segments.label: Choose Perceptron
segments.text: A perceptron represents a classifier with weights and a bias. It computes a linear score, compares the sign with a labeled target, and changes its parameters only when the prediction is wrong. Because one example can trigger one immediate update, the perceptron naturally supports online learning.

focuses.phrase: A perceptron represents a classifier with weights
focuses.label: Choose Perceptron

segments.label: Choose K-means
segments.text: K-means represents each cluster by a centroid. It receives no class labels; instead, distance supplies the signal by assigning each point to its nearest centroid and then moving that centroid to the group mean. Those alternating batch steps continue until the assignments or centroids stabilize.

focuses.phrase: K-means represents each cluster by a centroid.
focuses.label: Choose K-means

segments.label: Choose Reinforcement learning
segments.text: Reinforcement learning represents behavior with a policy or value function. An agent acts, observes consequences, and receives delayed rewards rather than a correct label for every move. The timing is sequential: today’s action can change tomorrow’s state, so credit assignment must connect outcomes back to earlier decisions.

focuses.phrase: Reinforcement learning represents behavior with a policy
focuses.label: Choose Reinforcement learning

slides.title: Symbolic structures and numeric representations change differently

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Symbolic learning changes explicit structures: a decision-tree test, a branch, a concept description, or a rule cutoff. The learned object names relationships in a form a person can often read directly.

focuses.phrase: Symbolic learning changes explicit structures: a decision-tree
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Symbolic learning changes explicit structures: a decision-tree
kinetics.label: Symbolic structures and numeric representations change differently

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Non-symbolic learning adapts numeric representations such as weights, centroids, embeddings, or fitness-driven parameters. Meaning is distributed through numbers and geometry rather than written as one if-then sentence.

focuses.phrase: Non-symbolic learning adapts numeric representations such as
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Do not mistake symbolic for rigid and numeric for intelligent. Both can adapt and overfit. The practical questions are what changes smoothly, what can be explained, and which patterns the representation makes easy or impossible.

focuses.phrase: Do not mistake symbolic for rigid and
focuses.label: Mechanism

slides.title: The same loan task can use rules or a weighted boundary

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: A decision tree might learn, if income is low, predict high risk. The test and branch are explicit. A case near a cutoff may jump to another route because the rule treats the two sides as different symbols.

focuses.phrase: A decision tree might learn, if income
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: A decision tree might learn, if income
kinetics.label: The same loan task can use rules or a weighted boundary

segments.label: Define
segments.text: A perceptron computes the sign of w transpose x plus b. Every feature contributes through a weight, and the equation defines one boundary. Moving a weight rotates the boundary; moving bias shifts it.

focuses.phrase: A perceptron computes the sign of w
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Both models can use the same labels yet encode the solution differently. The tree explains a path of conditions; the perceptron explains a signed score and a geometric side. Same homework, different handwriting—and different limits.

focuses.phrase: Both models can use the same labels
focuses.label: Mechanism

slides.title: Genetic programming evolves functions that fit labeled values

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Genetic programming represents candidate solutions as expression trees. Internal nodes are functions such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, or protected division; leaves are variables and constants. Changing the tree changes the program.

focuses.phrase: Genetic programming represents candidate solutions as expression
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Genetic programming represents candidate solutions as expression
kinetics.label: Genetic programming evolves functions that fit labeled values

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Evaluation runs each candidate on all labeled pairs. A fitness function summarizes prediction error, so smaller error means a better fit here. Fitness is the selection signal, not proof that the expression discovered a true law.

focuses.phrase: Evaluation runs each candidate on all labeled
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Tournament selection samples four candidates and favors a fitter parent. Crossover swaps subtrees with ninety percent probability; mutation changes material with five percent probability while depth limits prevent algebraic spaghetti.

focuses.phrase: Tournament selection samples four candidates and favors
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: The loop stops at error zero point zero zero one or generation one hundred. Evolution searches heuristically; it does not enumerate every program or guarantee the globally best tree.

focuses.phrase: The loop stops at error zero point
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Fitness design defines evolutionary success. Mean absolute error treats a one-unit miss linearly; squared error punishes large misses more; a complexity penalty can discourage enormous trees that shave tiny training errors. Selection optimizes the declared score, not an abstract notion of elegance. If the objective rewards the wrong behavior, evolution can become creative at doing precisely the wrong thing.

focuses.phrase: Fitness design defines evolutionary success. Mean absolute
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Worked detail
segments.text: Imagine two parents: one tree encodes x times x and another encodes x divided by two. Crossover can exchange a subtree to produce x times x divided by two, while mutation might replace a constant. The child is not guaranteed better; evaluation decides. Variation proposes, fitness judges, selection changes which proposals are more likely to reproduce.

focuses.phrase: Imagine two parents: one tree encodes x
focuses.label: Worked detail

segments.label: Represent
segments.text: Genetic programming begins by representing candidate programs as expression trees assembled from variables, constants, and allowed functions. This is the search language: if an operation is absent from the building set, evolution cannot magically invent it.

focuses.phrase: Genetic programming begins by representing candidate programs
focuses.label: Represent

segments.label: Evaluate
segments.text: Evaluation runs every candidate on all ten labeled pairs and converts aggregate prediction error into fitness. A lower training error earns reproductive preference, but it is not a diploma in universal truth; generalization still needs separate evidence.

focuses.phrase: Evaluation runs every candidate on all ten
focuses.label: Evaluate

segments.label: Select
segments.text: Selection now samples four candidates for a tournament and favors the fittest member as a parent. This creates useful pressure without globally sorting the entire population, like holding many small auditions instead of one enormous talent show.

focuses.phrase: Selection now samples four candidates for a
focuses.label: Select

segments.label: Vary
segments.text: Variation creates new programs. Crossover swaps subtrees with ninety percent probability, mutation makes smaller changes with five percent probability, and depth limits keep the trees from becoming botanical monsters that are impressive but useless.

focuses.phrase: Variation creates new programs. Crossover swaps subtrees
focuses.label: Vary

segments.label: Stop
segments.text: Termination makes the computational budget explicit. Search ends when error reaches zero point zero zero one or after one hundred generations, whichever comes first; otherwise evolution could keep tinkering like a chef who refuses to serve dinner.

focuses.phrase: Termination makes the computational budget explicit. Search
focuses.label: Stop

segments.text: Trace units as a consistency check. Input x has its original scale; squaring creates x squared; dividing by two produces the target scale. An expression x divided by two may match endpoints loosely but misses the curvature. Comparing residuals across all rows reveals that distinction more reliably than admiring one successful prediction.

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Step one constructs X as ten rows with one feature and y as matching targets. Reshape matters because estimator interfaces expect examples by rows and features by columns.

focuses.phrase: Step one constructs X as ten rows
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Step one constructs X as ten rows
kinetics.label: A symbolic regressor follows a fit and predict workflow

segments.label: Define
segments.text: Step two configures population six hundred, one hundred generations, and tournament size four. These settings control search effort and pressure; they do not change the meaning of fit or predict.

focuses.phrase: Step two configures population six hundred, one
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Step three calls fit. Behind the familiar interface, the library evolves expression trees instead of solving ordinary linear regression. Printing the selected program exposes the surviving expression.

focuses.phrase: Step three calls fit. Behind the familiar
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Step four predicts unseen values and measures error. Precision point: gplearn is scikit-learn-compatible, not a core scikit-learn estimator. Familiar packaging should not blur the actual algorithm.

focuses.phrase: Step four predicts unseen values and measures
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: The fit-predict interface separates training from inference. Fit inspects X and y and alters the estimator. Predict receives only new X and uses the learned program without target access. Evaluation compares predictions with withheld y. Keeping these roles separate prevents leakage and makes experiments reproducible across symbolic regression, trees, and numeric estimators.

focuses.phrase: The fit-predict interface separates training from inference.
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Show data step
segments.text: The data stage separates inputs from targets. X contains ten rows with one feature each, while y contains the ten matching regression values that supply supervised feedback.

focuses.phrase: The data stage separates inputs from targets.
focuses.label: Show data step

segments.label: Show model step
segments.text: The model stage configures the evolutionary search: population size controls how many candidate programs compete, generations limit how long evolution runs, and tournament size controls selection pressure.

focuses.phrase: The model stage configures the evolutionary search:
focuses.label: Show model step

segments.label: Show fit step
segments.text: During fitting, the estimator keeps a familiar scikit-style interface, but its internal optimizer is evolving expression trees rather than solving directly for numeric coefficients. Familiar packaging can hide a very different learning mechanism.

focuses.phrase: During fitting, the estimator keeps a familiar
focuses.label: Show fit step

segments.label: Show test step
segments.text: Testing asks the evolved program to predict values it did not optimize directly. That distinction matters because excellent training fitness can belong to an overgrown expression that generalizes about as well as a horoscope.

focuses.phrase: Testing asks the evolved program to predict
focuses.label: Show test step

slides.title: An artificial neuron combines weighted inputs, bias, and activation

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: An artificial neuron receives inputs x sub i. Each input is multiplied by weight w sub i, and the neuron adds the contributions: net equals the sum of w sub i x sub i plus bias.

focuses.phrase: An artificial neuron receives inputs x sub
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: An artificial neuron receives inputs x sub
kinetics.label: An artificial neuron combines weighted inputs, bias, and activation

segments.label: Define
segments.text: A positive weight makes larger input push upward; a negative weight pushes downward. Magnitude controls influence. A zero weight tells that feature, thank you for coming, your contribution is nothing.

focuses.phrase: A positive weight makes larger input push
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Bias is a constant input of one with its own weight. It shifts the decision point without changing measured features, like moving a ruler's zero mark.

focuses.phrase: Bias is a constant input of one
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Activation converts net to output. A hard step yields a class-like decision; sigmoid yields a smooth value; later networks use differentiable activations so error can guide many weights.

focuses.phrase: Activation converts net to output. A hard
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Expand the equation with two features: net equals w one x one plus w two x two plus b. This is affine. Before activation, equal-score points lie on parallel lines, and the zero-score set is the decision boundary. The diagram is both a signal-aggregating circuit and a geometric machine assigning each point to a side.

focuses.phrase: Expand the equation with two features: net
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

slides.title: Change one factor and watch the score cross threshold

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: Begin with inputs zero point eight and zero point four, weights zero point seven and negative zero point three, and bias negative zero point two. Net is zero point eight times zero point seven plus zero point four times negative zero point three minus zero point two, or zero point two four.

focuses.phrase: Begin with inputs zero point eight and
focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.phrase: Begin with inputs zero point eight and

segments.label: Define
segments.text: The hard activation returns one when net is at least zero, so this setting outputs one. The second feature subtracts because its weight is negative.

focuses.phrase: The hard activation returns one when net
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: Changing one value isolates its role. Reducing w one weakens positive evidence; making bias more negative shifts every example toward zero. Predict the direction before moving the control, then inspect the score.

focuses.phrase: Changing one value isolates its role. Reducing
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: Crossing zero creates a discrete jump even when a slider moves smoothly. That is useful for threshold logic but problematic when we need a gradient saying how to improve a mistake.

focuses.phrase: Crossing zero creates a discrete jump even
focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Calculate initial contributions separately: the first gives positive zero point five six, the second negative zero point one two, and bias negative zero point two. Their sum is positive zero point two four. A contribution ledger prevents a common error—changing one weight and mentally changing every term as if one slider had union representation.

focuses.phrase: Calculate initial contributions separately: the first gives
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Worked detail
segments.text: Now separate boundary movement from evidence movement. Adjusting x changes the current case's location while holding the model fixed. Adjusting w or bias changes the model while holding the case fixed. Both alter net, but they answer different questions: what if this input were different, versus what if the learned decision rule were different?

focuses.phrase: Now separate boundary movement from evidence movement.
focuses.label: Worked detail

segments.label: Reduce the first weight
segments.text: Weight one is now only zero point one, so the first feature contributes much less positive evidence. The total score crosses below zero, and the hard-threshold output switches off. A weight controls influence, not the feature value itself.

focuses.phrase: Weight one is now only zero point
focuses.label: Reduce the first weight

segments.label: Raise the bias
segments.text: The bias now rises to zero point two. Because bias is a constant offset, it lifts the score for every input combination, bringing this example back across the threshold and switching the output on.

focuses.phrase: The bias now rises to zero point
focuses.label: Raise the bias

segments.label: Make the second weight positive
segments.text: Weight two is now positive zero point six. The second feature changes from subtracting evidence to adding it, so the net score increases. The sign of a weight tells us the direction of influence.

focuses.phrase: Weight two is now positive zero point
focuses.label: Make the second weight positive

segments.label: Lower the first input
segments.text: The first input is now negative zero point five. With a positive first weight, that feature contributes a negative product and pulls the score downward. Here the evidence changed while the model stayed fixed.

focuses.phrase: The first input is now negative zero
focuses.label: Lower the first input

slides.title: Fixed weights and bias implement AND and OR

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: For both gates, set input weights to one and use a hard threshold at net zero. AND uses bias negative two, so only one plus one minus two reaches zero; the other three pairs stay negative.

focuses.label: Frame

kinetics.label: Fixed weights and bias implement AND and OR

segments.label: Define
segments.text: OR uses bias negative one, so either single one reaches zero and one-one is positive. Only zero-zero stays negative. The weights are unchanged; bias moves the threshold.

focuses.phrase: OR uses bias negative one, so either
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: These McCulloch-Pitts units are engineered, not learned. Someone selected parameters to reproduce truth tables. We will run every pair so the equation—not a memorized slogan—shows why the gates differ.

focuses.phrase: These McCulloch-Pitts units are engineered, not learned.
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Write the AND inequalities. Zero-zero, one-zero, and zero-one must score below zero; one-one must score at least zero. Unit weights and bias negative two satisfy all four. For OR only zero-zero must stay below zero, so bias negative one works. Bias encodes how much combined evidence is required.

focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Frame
segments.text: For AND at zero-zero, net is negative two and output zero. With one input active, net is negative one, still zero. With both active, net reaches zero and output becomes one.

focuses.label: Frame

segments.label: Define
segments.text: For OR, bias changes to negative one. Zero-zero produces negative one, either single one produces zero, and one-one produces positive one.

focuses.phrase: For OR, bias changes to negative one.
focuses.label: Define

segments.label: Mechanism
segments.text: The invariant is weights one and one. The changed bias determines which truth-table corners cross the same threshold. A gate is a tiny geometric classifier over four points.

focuses.phrase: The invariant is weights one and one.
focuses.label: Mechanism

segments.label: Interpret
segments.text: We will demonstrate all combinations. Watching the score update transfers better to larger feature vectors than chanting AND needs both.

focuses.label: Interpret

segments.label: Deepen
segments.text: Notice the equality convention. Activation returns one when net is greater than or equal to zero, not strictly greater. That is why AND at one-one with net exactly zero turns on, and OR with a single active input turns on. Changing the comparison operator would require changing bias or would alter boundary cases.

focuses.phrase: Notice the equality convention. Activation returns one
focuses.label: Detailed explanation

segments.label: Worked detail
segments.text: List AND in order: zero-zero gives negative two, zero-one negative one, one-zero negative one, one-one zero. OR gives negative one, zero, zero, one. The two tables differ only in the three middle score offsets created by bias. Writing the numbers makes the mechanism portable to any pair of binary inputs.
